title: Adaptive Reserve Fallback and Tenant Grace Mechanism
creator: Amira Patel
description: Define and ship an adaptive fallback mechanism for Dedicated reserved pools that gracefully degrades tenant throughput during transient capacity shortfalls while preserving predictable SLAs for committed customers. This PRD covers policy definition, crediting/grace mechanics, observability, rollout strategy and acceptance criteria.
background: We frequently observe short-lived capacity storms where committed reserved pools temporarily lack headroom for tenant bursts. Current hard preemption or immediate fallback to lower-tier models causes abrupt latency spikes and poor customer experience. We need a mechanism that buys time for autoscale and headroom rebalancing while preserving fairness across tenants and minimizing cost impact.
goals: Provide a bounded, auditable grace window (soft fallback) for committed tenants during transient shortages
Ensure fallbacks are reversible and non-destructive to active requests and KV caches
Expose controls for operators and customers to tune grace behavior and visibility
Maintain median and p95 latency SLAs for committed tenants within defined tolerances
Minimize additional unit cost compared to current autoscale behavior (< ~10% estimated)
scope_in: Policy engine to issue tenant-specific soft grace credits tied to reserved pools
Tenant credit ledger (ephemeral) and consumption accounting
Fallback routing to compatible, lower-cost model variants or degraded QoS profiles
Console controls: enable/disable, per-tenant grace budget, observability panels
Operator alerts and runbook integration for grace exhaustion and manual escalation
scope_out: Major changes to billing metering (billing will read ledger but maintain current invoices)
Cross-region routing policy changes beyond emergency fallback scope
New quantization pipelines; model conversion to support degraded variants is handled by separate model onboarding work
Customer self-serve negotiation of contract terms (handled by Sales/legal)
requirements: R1: Grace window provisioning — platform may grant a time-limited grace credit to tenants in the affected reserved pool with configurable budget (seconds of tokens or concurrent capacity)
R2: Prioritization — credits should prefer tenants with active recent usage and high entitlement, with deterministic tie-breakers (priority epochs + recent token rate)
R3: Non-destructive eviction — in-flight requests must either complete on current capacity or be gracefully routed to fallback variants without corrupting KV caches where possible
R4: Observability — per-tenant ledger, consumed credits, grace start/end events, and reason codes must be recorded and surfaced in Console and logs
R5: Operator controls — ability to forcibly drain, extend, or revoke grace for a tenant via Console and API with audit logs
R6: Autoscale handshake — grace mechanism must integrate with autoscaler signals (target headroom, prewarm triggers) to avoid double-scaling and ensure rapid recovery
R7: Configurability — defaults for grace duration, budget and downgrade profiles, with per-tenant overrides for enterprise customers
R8: Safety — platform must enforce a global hard limit (absolute max grace across pool) to prevent runaway cost and ensure fairness
acceptance_criteria: AC1: In a staged load test simulating 3x baseline sudden burst, 95% of committed-tenant requests receive either original model or graceful fallback with no request-level error (HTTP 5xx) > 0.5%
AC2: Grace ledger reports correct consumption: ledger entries match observed token consumption within 3% in synthetic tests
AC3: Automated fallback reversal occurs within configured recovery window after autoscaler signals restored headroom in >= 98% of test runs
AC4: Console telemetry shows per-tenant grace usage and exposes a filterable incidents view; PM/Design sign-off on UX flows
AC5: Operator forced-revoke action revokes current grace within 5s and is logged to audit trail
AC6: End-to-end cost delta for affected pools during test scenarios is < 10% compared to baseline autoscale-only runs
AC7: Security review completed and design passes internal compliance checklist (encryption of ledger entries in transit & at rest)
metrics: M1: Grace use rate = % of capacity-short events that trigger at least one grace grant
M2: Recovery latency = time from grace start to restore-to-native-capacity (seconds)
M3: Fallback success rate = % of requests that complete successfully via fallback profile
M4: Cost delta = additional GPU-minutes consumed when grace active vs autoscale baseline
M5: Customer satisfaction proxy = % of committed tenants with no SLA breach during event
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal alpha) — implement stub policy and ledger, run cluster-local chaos tests with internal tenants (1 week)
Phase 1 (canary) — enable for 3 low-risk committed tenants across 2 pools; monitor for 2 weeks with tight guardrails and rollback flag
Phase 2 (expanded) — increase to 20% of committed tenants in non-production pools, add alerting and cost dashboards (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (select production) — opt-in for enterprise customers by request with sales coordination (4 weeks)
Phase 4 (global rollout) — enable defaults with soft opt-out and customer notification (2 weeks)
risks: RISK1: Incorrect credit accounting could lead to billing disputes — mitigation: double-write audits and reconciliation job
RISK2: Overuse of grace across many tenants increases unit cost — mitigation: global hard cap and operator alerts
RISK3: Fallback model variants may produce unacceptable quality regressions — mitigation: require per-variant evals and gated rollout
RISK4: Complex interactions with existing autoscale may cause thrashing — mitigation: define explicit autoscale handshake and backoff window
RISK5: UX confusion for customers about why fallbacks occurred — mitigation: customer-facing incident messages + console explanations
decisions: DECISION1: Use time-limited credit (seconds/token-equivalent) rather than artificial concurrency slots to simplify accounting
DECISION2: Fallback profiles will be pre-approved model variants of the same architecture where possible; cross-architecture fallbacks are last-resort
DECISION3: Default grace budget = 90s equivalent of median request tokens for the tenant; enterprise tenants may request > budget
DECISION4: Audit logs and ledger entries will be encrypted and retained for 90 days by default
